neighbours.label: the start of a reported answer after 'told <someone>' or 'said' in a question-and-answer story: the ' it' / ' was' in "she asked who that was, and I told her [it] was my sister"; not a plain 'it was' statement with no report
fire: My cousin asked me who the tall woman was, and I told him it was our new teacher.
When the nurse asked whose coat it was, I told her it was my father's.
The boy wanted to know what the smell was, so we told him it was the paint.
A neighbour asked who had been at the door, and she told them it was the postman.
Somebody asked me what that noise was, and I told her it was only the fridge.
The officer asked who owned the van, and I told him it was my uncle.
My daughter asked what the light in the sky was, and I told her it was a planet.
They asked us who had left the gate open, and we told them it was the gardener.
quiet: My cousin and I met the tall woman, and it was our new teacher.
The nurse picked up the coat, and it was my father's.
The boy noticed the smell at once, and it was the paint.
A neighbour went to the door, and it was the postman.
Somebody switched off that noise, and it was only the fridge.
The officer looked at the van, and it was full of boxes.
My daughter watched the light in the sky until it was gone.
They closed the gate again because it was getting dark.

notes: Card: no single token and 0.88% of tokens reach 0.1 of max, so this label can only be a part of the pole. The top story example is 'a friend asked me who that lady was... I told her [it] was my sister'. Probes: 'I told him it was my brother' 0.48, 'he said it was the bank' 0.32, 'we told her it was the wind' 0.21, 'I told him I was lost' 0.19; 'In this paper, we' 0.05, 'I saw a dog' 0.08, plain 'It was the wind that' 0.05. Near misses keep the people and the 'it was' but drop the reported answer.
